extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and news editors (readers of wire dispatches)
extracted.subtask_description: Writing and publishing frontline wartime news dispatches that summarize military actions, cite official communiqués and field reports, and balance factual reporting with acknowledgement of uncertainty. Emphasis on datelines, sourcing, and precise geographic/military details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Attribute information to its source (e.g., 'the headquarters communique declared', 'Associated Press correspondent', 'field dispatches said', 'the Chinese communist radio said', 'a pilot returning from the front said').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always specify where a fact came from (official communique, field correspondent, pilot, enemy radio). Examples in text: repeated attributions to 'HEADQUARTERS', 'FIELD DISPATCHES', 'ASSOCIATED PRESS CORRESPONDENT', and 'COMMUNIST RADIO'. Avoid presenting unattributed claims as fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish confirmed vs unconfirmed reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Flag when reports are unofficial or unconfirmed (e.g., 'UNOFFICIAL REPORTS ... WERE NOT CONFIRMED', 'IT WAS NOT KNOWN AT HEADQUARTERS WHETHER ...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label rumors or preliminary reports explicitly and avoid asserting them as fact. Use language such as 'reported', 'unconfirmed', or 'apparently' as shown in the communique and field dispatches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include datelines and timestamps
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide dateline and time context for dispatches and official texts (e.g., 'TOKYO, SATURDAY JULY 15', 'issued at 3210 P.M., JAPAN DAYLIGHT TIME (12210 P.M., FRIDAY, EST)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give readers when and where a report or communique was released to establish currency and provenance of information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise geographic detail and distances
rubrics_metrics.description: Give specific locations and distances (e.g., '20 miles northwest of Taejon', 'about 65 air miles northeast of Taejon', '200-yard-wide river').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use named places, directional bearings and distances to orient readers; the article repeatedly specifies towns, river segments and mileages to clarify where actions occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use direct quotations for official wording
rubrics_metrics.description: Quote phrasing from official communiques or spokesmen verbatim when notable (e.g., 'A SETBACK' but 'NO CAUSE FOR UNDUE ALARM', 'HOLD AT ANY COST').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve and quote striking or authoritative official language; this both informs and preserves the source's tone and claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify military units and force composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Name divisions, regiments and unit identities and, when possible, note strength (e.g., 'North Korean Sixth Division', '34th Infantry Regiment', 'elements of the ... Second Division crossed the Pogang River').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report unit identifications and movements; if strength is unknown, state that (the text often notes 'strength unknown').

rubrics_metrics.name: Report matériel, losses and sortie counts with attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide counts of equipment destroyed/damaged or sorties flown, but attribute them (e.g., 'six enemy tanks were reported destroyed and seven damaged', 'approximately 190 flights', '37 trucks were destroyed and 55 damaged').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantitative claims should be attributed to a reporting source and qualified when necessary (e.g., 'were reported', 'results ... not known'). Avoid standalone numeric assertions without source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corroborate via multiple reporting streams
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and compare communiques, field dispatches, pilot reports and enemy broadcasts to form the narrative (the piece juxtaposes HQ communiques, field dispatches, pilots' returns and enemy radio claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-check and present multiple perspectives; when reports conflict, present them with their sources and note discrepancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate factual reporting from analysis/opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish straight dispatch details from interpretive passages (e.g., news paragraphs describing troop behavior vs. analysis: 'The Reds have shown smart tactics...' and comparisons to historical battles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear which sentences are factual updates and which are analyst or editorial interpretation; readers should be able to tell reporting from commentary.
